docs.text: Rivers and lakes are amazing. I mean, I love an ocean but something about a river flowing to its destination, or a massive lake like Lake Michigan and even a small lake and a pontoon ride. Water is the life giver. #EarthDay
Lake Michigan this morning from just off the shores of Milwaukee, Wisconsin I'll never take for granted living alongside an entire ocean of fresh water...
The same place four months apart. If I could have a superpower I would want to be able to breathe underwater and swim comfortably in any conditions and to see in the dark.
The lakefront in Kenosha is wonderful, and might as well be the ocean. Spent countless hours right here as a teenager

See, this is one of the reasons I continue to live in one of the most expensive places on the planet. The ocean is 2 miles from my house. I grew up with Lake Michigan 2 blocks from my house but the ocean … the ocean is just a whole other thing
The specific thing that I am an evangelist for is Lake Michigan. Everything you could want from the ocean except it's pure fresh water. You haven't lived until you've gone swimming in Lake Michigan.

I’ve lived 2 miles from the Pacific Ocean for 30 years. Before that I lived 2 blocks from Lake Michigan for 18 years. I can’t imagine a life without a giant body of water outside my doorstep. Inland seems like an alien world
We're here for water, but land is cool too.
I grew up by the English Channel and miss its moods every day after 57 years. I can see and hear Lake Huron but somehow it’s not the same. Probably because the salty smell is missing.

As an alaskan in california feel this. I have never lived away from the ocean though and the thought of nothing but land for miles in all directions with no end point kind of freaks me out (I bet the great lakes remedy that though)
Realizing I haven't not lived near a giant body of water my entire life. Lake Huron, Lake Michigan, Pacific Ocean, Lake Michigan. I'm just used to always seeing water on my local weather maps

I can get the bush totally … for me it’s the ocean, or at the very least a body of water. But really it’s about having a beach nearby. There’s something about large bodies of water that centres me. Even in Chicago I had Lake Michigan about a 10-15 min walk from my apartment.

I've sailed my whole life in Seattle area. When we came to Wisconsin, we scared the shit out of ourselves with Green Bay weather changes....and that was with 'accurate' forecasts. We don't go far in our sailboat anymore out of 'respect' for Lake Michigan.
I make a lot of jokes about how the Lake Michigan shore isn't a "real" beach. But secretly I'm very glad to be so far away from the ocean.

I lived on a small island in MI. Garden island, uninhabited, owned by the DNR. Lake Michigan was my bathtub and drinking water for 6 weeks. Grew up 2 blocks from Atwater beach, went on over night sails on da lake. The ocean is a whole other thing, there is just no comparison

Oh. Neptune conj MC and I have always tried to live on or near water. Lake Superior and Michigan mostly but any lake, pond, or body of water will do in a pinch. If I'm traveling, it's to spend time by/in as much water as possible
Yes. I’m such an ocean girl. From the Midwest. Lake Michigan is close.

I get that. I’m about 1000km from the sea now, and having lived most of my life within 1000 steps of it, I miss it like crazy! The Great Lakes are impressive, but they just can’t replace the smell and sound of the sea.
I can feel that. I live where I was born, between 2 of the Great Lakes. They aren’t the ocean but I make do.

i feel like for the metabolically active cells, your kidney cells, etc you're fully local within a month or two, but there's pockets of cells with longer lives that would hold on to their water. i have seven years of being away from the great lakes water table and maybe i still feel them somewhere

I haven't actually had that much exposure to the ocean, but I like it in theory. I live in Great Lakes territory. The only times I've been in the ocean are in PEI and England. Cold and kind of smelly. But the trio of tattoos on my inner bicep represent my grandparents, who were/are ocean people.
Haven't visited Gulf in over 40 years, most of my time on beach is Lake Michigan or Lake Superior.

I've always been a Pacific Coast girl. From Japan, to SoCal, to Central CA, to Oregon Coast girl... There's nothing like the great Pacific! Never even seen the Atlantic. And I've only been to the Western Shore of Lake Erie. I really need to change that. 💯
I live on Lake Superior, not the ocean, but I don’t think I’ll ever live land-bound again.

I didn’t realise how important the proximity of the sea was to me until I moved to the middle of America, and lived on the shores of Lake Michigan. It’s not like I’m always at the seaside here, but it’s just knowing it’s right there.

My home country is a smallish rock in the North Atlantic, buffeted on the west by 3,000-mile waves. I spent 5 months living in a Canadian provincial park on the north shore of Lake Superior The moods of a big lake are far more mysterious to me than ocean tides.
I love oceans (and inland seas like Lake Superior). I live nowhere near any, but love the pull of them whenever I get there

I miss living on or even near the coast. I’m on Lake Ontario, as big as a sea, with waves nearly as large as anywhere at times, but it is not the same as the ocean. Salt air, sea breeze, heavy fog, tide pools, even the sound is different. Your skin and hair after a dip in salt water. I miss it all.

I get that! I grew up on the Atlantic coast...I could see the ocean from my bedroom window. Then lived on the shore of Lake Ontario for years. Now in Guelph an hour and a half from any big water! Miss the water!
I live right on Lake Michigan. Being near the water just helps your soul.

Moving close to an ocean has been one of the best life choices ever. It’s also made me double down on my love for Lake Michigan, which I grew up reasonably near. Honorary sea tbh. I hope you find your stream, woods, or other neat little nature place of some kind.
I love living near water, or mountains. Lake Michigan thinks it's an ocean, and brings joy daily.

Being near water is important to me, too. I see you (as the kids say). I grew up on the shores of the Great Lakes, and now I live in Oregon, on the coast where water is abundant. Such a blessing. Peace.
Also have never been near an ocean... But the Great Lakes are very nearby, so I'm good ;)
Bahahaha you’re cute! I have you filled an ocean and 5 Great Lakes away😉🤭😄
I love everything ocean!! I grew up by the Great Lakes, unsalted and gorgeous …nothing more beautiful than waves on a shore.
I have lived all over the US, mostly East Coast, now Great Lakes. Mermaids 🧜‍♂️ 🧜‍♀️ & Murmen are drawn to the seas 🌊 💙⚓️🔱⚜️👑🐝
Awesome! That explains a lot. The ocean's always felt like home to me. I wish I lived closer to it. I do live near the Great Lakes, though. :)
i think people who grew up nearish to an ocean or other major body of water (great lakes, huge rivers, etc) have a stronger sense of “towards the ocean/water” than cardinal directions.

You and me both. I live inland now, with Lake Ontario being the closest thing to a seashore. It's not the same. I first went to sea in 1990 and it's been a central part of my career ever since. I got out out of the Navy and went into seismic exploration so fully 1/4 of my life has been on the water.

I envy you. I grew up by the magestic pacific ocean and miss very much its sound, the salt on my skin, its smell. Very importantly also its bounty 🤤 the Great Lakes are wonderful too but they are not the ocean 😔
I only got "we have oceans at home" here (great lakes) :/
Trust me, I've lived next to Great Lakes and oceans (the Gulf)
I like finding neat rocks and sea glass and driftwood for art projects and stuff. The sea or Great Lakes breeze makes me feel grounded I guess too. I love mountains but am more a water type
I have lived on the shores of Great Lakes and on the Pacific Coast. They’re both beautiful, but different. Like the sun and the moon.

I am a daughter of both frost and seafoam; I was literally born during a sweeping polar vortex in Florida. Though I was raised in the north from a young age and spent summers in Michigan and Canada plunging myself into great lakes instead of the sea, there is something about the ocean
Uh oh, I don't see MA projecting into the ocean in that map. Perhaps I should move to the Great lakes, which are supposed to have a particularly stable climate.

Plus, anywhere that has the ocean can’t be *ALL* bad! Then again, I may be biased in favor of places with large bodies of water (though I do prefer mine to be unsalted and shark free 😁) (I also did a 30 days of riding in August 2015, as I was traveling around MI for work-hence the pictures!)
Oceans, The Great Lakes, and Mountains are my passions!
I long to live by a large body of water. Great Lakes specifically.
